Jane, Tom —

Thanks — attaching the documents now and addressing your questions inline below.

1) SOC 2: Attached is our most recent SOC 2 Type II report (Redwood-SOC2-report-2025.pdf). The report covers hosted API controls and our operational controls across the platform. Contact for SOC questions: Vivek Kulkarni (cc’d).

2) Subprocessor access to PII: In hosted deployments we process request payloads for inference. By default, request payloads are processed in-memory and persisted only to customer-scoped storage (S3) for logs and optional debug traces. We do not share customer PII with third parties for marketing or analytics. The attached CSV (redwood-subprocessors-20260220.csv) lists current subprocessors and a short purpose column. High-level:
- Amazon Web Services, Inc. — compute, object storage (S3) for optional logs and model artifacts.
- Google Cloud (optional region-specific storage) — used for regional failover per customer config.
- Cloudflare, Inc. — CDN and DDoS protection; no direct access to plaintext logs except for aggregated metrics.
- Datadog — observability (metrics and logs); logs are redacted by default and access-controlled.

3) Customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM): Yes — for Dedicated and Private deployments we support customer-managed keys (AWS KMS, customer-supplied HSM integrations) to encrypt persistent storage. Hosted customers can opt into customer-managed keys for storage encryption where contractual requirements apply.

4) Data retention & logs: Default retention for inference logs is 90 days; can be shortened via config. We retain audit logs for 1 year by default; retention policies can be adjusted for Dedicated/Private.

5) Encryption: All in-transit traffic is TLS 1.2+; at-rest encryption is AES-256. We can provide more granular crypto specs with Vivek.

6) Next step for the questionnaire: I’ve uploaded Vendor-Security-Questionnaire-Acme.xlsx and a shared Google Sheet link for collaborative completion: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1a2b3c-redwood-acme-questions. Vivek will own the questionnaire responses and can fill the technical controls section.

Attachments included: Redwood-SOC2-report-2025.pdf, redwood-subprocessors-20260220.csv, Vendor-Security-Questionnaire-Acme.xlsx

If that addresses the immediate asks, let’s confirm the Tue 24th 9am PT call to go through any follow-ups.

Best,

If you can answer those in the call we’ll be in good shape to move the vendor questionnaire forward. Also, please send the primary security contact and a time to hand off the questionnaire.
